_comment: Expectation manifest for conductor's frozen acceptance-checks.
Enforced repo-wide by scripts/evals-all.mjs on every push and PR.
expect "green" = a past fix that must not regress. MUST exit 0.
expect "red"   = a known-failing check (open concern). MUST exit 0 or 1.
A check file missing from this manifest FAILS the gate.
LOCKED (evals/**): improvement loops may never edit this file.

mutations.why: dropping STOP from the reject row lets a rejected task keep being worked instead of ending the turn
mutations.find: **STOP.** Do not implement, do not offer a smaller version.

mutations.why: dropping the hard-rules ban on a softened re-scope leaves only the routes-table wording, so a whetstone edit to one place silently loses the other
without this sentence, pushback on a reject reads as an invitation to retry the same task smaller — the exact softening this route exists to refuse
mutations.find: this one with the scope shaved down.

mutations.why: removing the hard-rule's 'no confirmation step' reopens the approval round-trip inline exists to remove
mutations.find: No confirmation step; the route already is the approval.

mutations.why: removing the routes-table's own denial of an approval round-trip leaves inline indistinguishable from lane in the one table a reader skims
mutations.find: No "should I proceed?", no approval round-trip.

mutations.why: an actual permission-seeking imperative inside inline's own prose is the real regression — the routing decision stops being the approval
mutations.replace: → ask the user for confirmation, then implement it, verify it

mutations.why: the routes-table row is the first thing a reader checks per route; losing 'ask before running it' there means lane reads as fire-and-forget
mutations.find: Freeze the DoD, print the `lirbox-builder` spawn and **ask before running it.**

mutations.why: losing the hard-rules restatement means only the table carries the rule, and printing the command could be read as already having acted
mutations.find: **`lane` always asks**, even though the spawn was already printed
mutations.replace: **`lane` prints the spawn**, ready to run

mutations.why: the `### lane` prose is where the actual instruction lives; without 'then ask' the printed command has no next step attached to it at all
dropping this turns step 1 back into an interrogation gate before intake ever runs, which is the exact multi-day-run failure mode intake was built to stop
mutations.find: Ask the user nothing before this.
mutations.replace: Confirm scope with the user before this.

mutations.why: removing the hard-rule leaves only the flow's step-1 wording as evidence, so an edit that reopens interrogation elsewhere in the skill goes unnoticed
without this line the `scope` route reads as license to ask the user directly instead of handing off to the planner, which is the interrogation path this skill exists to avoid
mutations.find: The fix is not five questions to the user — it is
mutations.replace: The fix is to ask the user a few questions, then it is

_note: The only check here that asserts against the ROUTER rather than the manual.
Its four siblings all read SKILL.md; none of them would go RED if decideRoute returned
'scope' forever, which is how the capability-outranks-reject bug shipped in aad48c7.
Proven RED on that baseline before the fix: assertion 1 failed, the three guard rails passed.

mutations.why: the reject branch stops returning its own route, so a 0.95-confidence refusal is handed to the planner to be cut smaller — the softened re-scope the route exists to refuse
the reject branch is never entered at all, so a confident refusal falls through to the bottom of the ladder and reads as permission to proceed
the capability gate stops outranking lane, so a prod-credential task buys a worktree this repo cannot give it — the over-broad fix that passes the invariant by deleting the guard rail
lowering the confidence bar lets an uncertain refusal become a verdict, so doubt buys the one route whose cost is that the work never happens at all

_note: decideRoute writes decided_by:'fallback' with route:'inline' when an answer is unusable
or jev dies. Both print the same route string as a measured go-ahead, so the skill has to
say which it got. Proven RED against SKILL.md at git HEAD before the fix, GREEN after.

mutations.why: the announce step stops naming decided_by at all, so an unmeasured route is reported with the same authority as a measured one
the reason the field matters is dropped, leaving an unexplained ritual that the next edit deletes as noise
mutations.find: a dead API key and a confident go-ahead are the same word on
mutations.replace: the route reads the same either way on

mutations.why: the hard-rules bullet stops denying that a fallback is a judgment, so only the flow step carries the rule and an edit to one place silently loses the other
a re-freeze overwrites the DoD, so the loop can rewrite its own finish line mid-run
mutations.find: if (existsSync(f)) die(`${slug} already has a frozen DoD
mutations.replace: if (false) die(`${slug} already has a frozen DoD

mutations.why: the hash is never compared, so a hand-loosened check is obeyed instead of refused
a checkable criterion with no command freezes — a wish that reads like a check
a cap on the number of criteria — the owner's rule is no cap, because a cap is how ticket ACs get dropped to fit
a fourth round is granted — the budget that made the old conductor stop is gone
the third failed round never records escalated, so the next gate call buys another round
an escalated run is re-gated instead of refused, so calling gate again buys rounds past the budget
docs stop counting toward the pass — met criteria alone pass a run with no record
a summary that is all frontmatter passes as a summary
the promoted implementation notes stop being required
a pass no longer writes the scorecard, so the frozen DoD and its verdicts never reach docs/changes
the implementor can rule on its own work — the self-report the verifier exists to replace
a verdict with no evidence is accepted — a bare yes from anyone
a verdict can overrule a checkable criterion's command
a missing verdict counts as met, so skipping the verifier passes the gate

mutations.replace: if (!v) return { id: c.id, tier: c.tier, met: true,

mutations.why: verdicts survive the round, so a ruling on pre-fix code passes the post-fix gate
the hard-rule making the gate the only done is dropped, so 'tests pass' reads as done
an escalated run may be reported as nearly done

mutations.why: phase workers are allowed back — the hand-off cost that lost every measured head-to-head
verification is no longer limited to one subagent

mutations.replace: If any criterion is `judged`, spawn reviewer agents, then
